text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated packet loss detected in eu1b affecting multiple inference clusters. Metrics: 5xx-rate +18%, p95 latency +420ms, retransmit spikes. Autochecks flagged host-level network queue saturation.
pagerduty: Triggered SRE page for oncall_ash (priority: P1). Pager link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-9876
oncall_ash: I'm on it. Joining. Can someone post the quick impact summary for product and customers?
infra_jon: Seeing BGP neighbors flapping on a subset of hosts in eu1b, and TCP retransmits in the kernel counters. Sample from one host: 
```
# cat /proc/net/snmp | grep Tcp
Tcp: RtoAlgorithm RtoMin RtoMax MaxConn ActiveOpens PassiveOpens AttemptFails EstabResets CurrEstab InSeg OutSeg RetransSeg
Tcp: 1 200 120000 - 12345 678 12 3 4567 98000 120000 540
```
Also traceroute to endpoint shows large jumps at the AZ's NLB.
sre_maya: Confirmed inference rqps dropped ~22% for that fleet and tail latency spikes. Canary evals show low quality errors due to truncated responses. Attempting instance-level drain on 2 problematic hosts to reduce noisy neighbors.
ops_leah: Starting traffic steering policy to avoid eu1b for non-data-local routed customers. Will update DNS weighted routing and add temporary route to eu1a and eu2a. ETA for DNS propagation ~45s after change.
support_elaine: Notifying affected customers who have dedicated eu1b capacity and warn about increased latency. Draft message: "We are mitigating a network degradation in eu1b; we are steering traffic to nearby AZs and you may see higher latency/brief request retries." Approving and sending to customers with SLA watch.
oncall_ash: infra_jon, can you confirm if this is instance NIC / ENI exhaustion or upstream network fabric?
infra_jon: Looks like host NIC TX queue is saturated and we also see ENI attach throttling errors in Cloud logs for the region. Cloud console shows limited capacity for certain instance types in eu1b (GPUs). Provisioned-on-demand attempts failing with InsufficientInstanceCapacity: "NoAvailableInstances".
sre_maya: Plan: 1) Drain and reboot the 6 hosts with NIC errors. 2) Ramp routing away from eu1b for stateless inference endpoints. 3) For dedicated customers pinned to eu1b, spin up standby in eu1a and ask for live failover where possible. 4) Enable progressive retries and increase client timeouts to avoid tail errors.
infra_jon: Rebooting host i-eu1b-03 now. Log: 
```
[2024-06-12T09:22:13Z] Reboot initiated by infra_jon
[2024-06-12T09:22:28Z] NIC reset, link flapped
[2024-06-12T09:22:50Z] Host back, kernel tx queue drops reduced
```
ops_leah: DNS weighted change pushed: eu1b -> 10% weight, eu1a -> 60%, eu2a -> 30%. Cloud DNS update id: dns-change-7751. Rolling TTL is 30s.
pm_ryan: Product note: Canary traffic should prefer eu1a for model evals; please ensure ephemeral caches are warmed so customers don't see cold starts.
support_elaine: Customer A (dedicated) is impacted and on SLA watch. Opening a bridge with them.
oncall_ash: Good. Oncall handoff: I'll remain primary, infra_jon you'll take node remediation, ops_leah will own routing and DNS, support_elaine owns customer comms. Handoff recorded.
incident-bot: :information_source: Incident record created: INC-9876. Priority: P1. Runbook: network-degradation -> follow AZ-steer procedure.
ops_leah: After DNS change, global load shows successful offload from eu1b in 2 propagation cycles. Downstream: some requests still see elevated latency when they hit stateful sessions pinned to eu1b. Working on session migration hooks.
sre_maya: We observed one failing fallback: model-serving processes hitting 502 when upstream NLB responded slow. Quick mitigation: increase proxy timeouts and enable 503->retry logic in router for 5 minutes while steering finishes. Patching router now.
infra_jon: Noted: Attempts to request G5 capacity in eu1b returned InsufficientInstanceCapacity for 3 attempts. Spinning replacement capacity in eu1a using reserved pool. Command: 
```
redwood infra create-instance --region eu1a --type g5.x --tags "standby-for-eu1b"
```
Success for 2 instances. Queueing image sync.
oncall_ash: Any estimated time to restore normal p95?
sre_maya: If routing holds, p95 should drop to baseline in ~12-20 minutes once session migration completes. Node reboots are helping with retransmits.
support_elaine: Bridge established with Customer A, they accepted failover to eu1a and we scheduled a planned migration for their dedicated pool. They want ETA for rollback too.
pm_ryan: Please log any customer-facing config changes so we can include in post-incident report.
infra_jon: There are intermittent ENI attach throttles in the cloud provider control plane—filed ticket with provider (case #CP-33421). They've acknowledged capacity pressure in eu1b.
ops_leah: I've set a soft spindown for non-critical jobs in eu1b to free NIC bandwidth - rolling out via autoscale policy.
oncall_ash: Good. Keep updates here every 5 minutes. If any region flaps further, escalate to org-wide incident.
incident-bot: Paging: next escalation will notify Eng Team Leads in 10 minutes if unresolved.
sre_maya: Router timeout patch applied. Observability: p95 decreased 180ms in next 3m window. Error rate trending down but still above SLO.
infra_jon: Completed drains on 6 hosts; NIC stats stable. ENI throttle events still occasionally reported but much reduced.
ops_leah: DNS weights back to eu1a 50% eu2a 40% eu1b 10% as a conservative cap. No sign of cross-region failover loops.
support_elaine: Customer A migrated successfully. They reported transient retries but no data loss. Closing SLA watch for them.
oncall_ash: I'll run a quick blameless RCA checklist: timeline, root cause hypotheses (AZ capacity + NIC queue/ENI throttling), mitigations taken (drain/reboot, DNS steer, router timeouts, spin-up in eu1a), follow-ups (increase reserve pool, autoscale policy updates, add more aggressive session migration). Assigning owners.
pm_ryan: Add a product follow-up to ensure canary cache warming and cross-AZ warm pools for dedicated customers.
incident-bot: Incident state: Mitigated -> monitoring. Owners assigned, postmortem requested.
oncall_ash: Thanks team. If nothing else, I'll close the thread in 30m after stable metrics. :thumbsup:
